examples: can I go for a walk
answer: Walking every day is one of the best things you can do. Start slowly with short walks, speed doesn't matter, and build up a little at a time over the first 3 months. Stop and rest if you get short of breath, dizzy or have chest pain.
title: MedlinePlus · Heart bypass surgery, discharge

examples: is it ok to go up stairs
answer: Stairs are generally OK. Go slowly and rest halfway up if you need to.
title: MedlinePlus · Heart bypass surgery, discharge

examples: can I pick up my grandson
can I carry a laundry basket
answer: For the first 6 weeks, don't lift anything heavier than about 5 to 7 pounds. That's roughly a gallon of milk. Stop if you feel pulling on your breastbone. If your discharge papers give a different limit, follow your papers.
title: MedlinePlus · Heart bypass surgery, discharge

examples: can I reach over my head
can I push or pull things
how do I get out of a chair
answer: For the first 6 weeks, avoid reaching backward and don't let anyone pull on your arms, for example to help you up. When getting out of bed or a chair, keep your arms close to your sides. Stop if you feel pulling on your breastbone.
title: MedlinePlus · Heart bypass surgery, discharge

answer: Light tasks like setting the table or folding clothes are OK. Avoid even light housework for the first 2 to 3 weeks, and anything that strains your chest or arms, like vacuuming or mowing, until your surgeon says it's fine.
title: MedlinePlus · Heart bypass surgery, discharge

examples: can I go to the gym
can I use a rowing machine
can I ride an exercise bike
answer: Build activity up gradually over about 3 months, starting with walking. Avoid weightlifting and rowing machines that strain your chest. Ask your surgeon or cardiac rehab team before starting anything more intense.
title: MedlinePlus · Heart bypass surgery, discharge

answer: Cardiac rehab is a supervised program of exercise and education that helps you recover and lower your risk of future heart problems. If you were referred, it's worth doing. Your papers say the rehab office will call you to schedule.
title: NHLBI · What to expect after bypass surgery

examples: can I walk outside when it's cold
is it ok to walk in the heat
can I exercise outside in winter
can I walk outside in hot weather
can I exercise in the cold
answer: Avoid exercising outdoors when it's very hot or very cold. Indoor walking, like at a mall, is a good alternative.
title: MedlinePlus · Heart bypass surgery, discharge

examples: when can I start driving again
when can I get behind the wheel
answer: Don't drive for at least 4 to 6 weeks, and wait until your surgeon says it's OK. Your reflexes can be slow at first, and your breastbone needs to heal.
title: MedlinePlus · Heart bypass surgery, discharge

examples: when can I go back to work
can I return to my job
answer: Most people are off work for about 6 to 8 weeks, and many feel ready for light work somewhere between 6 and 12 weeks. A physically demanding job may take longer. Ask your surgeon when you can go back.
title: MedlinePlus · Heart bypass surgery, discharge

examples: can I go on a trip
when can I go on vacation
can I go out of town
answer: Avoid travel for at least 2 to 4 weeks after surgery, and check with your surgeon before any trip, especially a flight.
title: MedlinePlus · Heart bypass surgery, discharge

examples: can I have sex with my wife
can I sleep with my wife
answer: Sex is usually OK after about 2 to 4 weeks, once you feel comfortable. Ask your surgeon first, since your own recovery may differ.
title: American Heart Association · Recovering from heart surgery

examples: do I need someone with me
answer: It's best to have someone stay with you for at least the first 1 to 2 weeks at home.
title: MedlinePlus · Heart bypass surgery, discharge

examples: how do I wash my incision
can I get my incision wet
answer: Yes. Shower every day and gently wash your incisions with soap and water, then pat them dry. Avoid very hot water, which can make you dizzy.
title: MedlinePlus · Heart bypass surgery, discharge

examples: can I use a hot tub
can I go in the pool
can I soak in the tub
answer: Not yet. No baths, swimming or hot tubs until your incisions are fully healed. Showers are fine.
title: MedlinePlus · Heart bypass surgery, discharge

examples: can I put lotion on my incision
can I use cream on my scar
how do I take care of my incision
can I put powder on my incision
can I use oil on my scar
how should I clean my incision
how do I wash my scar
how do I take care of my stitches
answer: Wash your incision daily with soap and water and dry it gently. Don't put creams, lotions, powders or oils on it unless your care team says it's OK. Protect it from the sun.
title: MedlinePlus · Heart bypass surgery, discharge

answer: Itching, numbness or tingling around your incisions is common and can last 6 months or more. Redness, swelling, oozing or an opening is different: contact your care team about those.
title: MedlinePlus · Heart bypass surgery, discharge

examples: how do I care for my leg incision
do I need to wear my stocking
my leg where they took the vein
should my leg be up when I sit
how long do I wear compression socks
do I wear the stocking at night
answer: Keep the leg where the vein was taken raised when you sit, and wear your compression stocking during the day, usually for the first 2 to 3 weeks. Some swelling in that leg is normal for a few weeks.
title: MedlinePlus · Heart bypass surgery, discharge

examples: what foods are good for my heart
is fried chicken bad for me
answer: Aim for a heart-healthy diet: lots of vegetables, fruit, beans, nuts, whole grains, fish and lean protein, and less processed meat, refined carbs, sugary drinks and salt. An occasional treat is fine to ask your care team about.
title: AHA healthy diet guidelines (Healthwise)

examples: how much salt can I have
answer: Cutting back on salt helps your heart. The American Heart Association's ideal limit for most adults is 1,500 mg of sodium a day. Your care team may give you your own target.
title: AHA healthy diet guidelines (Healthwise)

examples: is a glass of wine ok
can I have a few drinks at a party
can I drink on the weekend
answer: Ask your care team first, because alcohol can interact with heart medicines. The American Heart Association's general advice is: if you don't drink, don't start, and if you do, keep it limited.
title: American Heart Association · Alcohol and heart health

examples: is a cup of coffee in the morning ok
how much coffee can I have
answer: Your discharge papers don't mention caffeine, and I don't have a trusted source to give you a limit. Ask your care team, especially since metoprolol affects your heart rate.

examples: is grapefruit bad with my statin
answer: Grapefruit can interact with atorvastatin. MedlinePlus advises talking to your doctor about grapefruit and grapefruit juice while you take it.
title: MedlinePlus · Atorvastatin

examples: is it normal to not be hungry
answer: A low appetite is common for several weeks after bypass surgery and usually improves. Try small, frequent meals. If you can't keep food or fluids down, contact your care team.
title: NHLBI · What to expect after bypass surgery

examples: I haven't had a bowel movement in days
answer: Constipation is common after surgery, partly from pain medicine and moving less. Ask your care team before taking a stool softener or laxative.
title: NHLBI · What to expect after bypass surgery

examples: how much water should I drink
how much should I drink a day
answer: Your papers don't give a fluid amount. Some heart patients have a fluid limit, so ask your care team for yours. Daily weigh-ins help them spot fluid buildup.

Please don't smoke. Studies of bypass patients found that people who kept smoking had a much higher risk of death than people who quit. Quitting at any point helps. Your care team can help with a quit plan.
title: CardioSmart (ACC) · Quitting smoking after heart surgery

answer: Low-dose aspirin helps keep blood clots from forming, which lowers the risk of a heart attack or stroke. Don't stop it unless your heart doctor says so.
title: MedlinePlus · Aspirin

answer: Metoprolol is a beta blocker. It slows your heart rate and lowers blood pressure so your heart works less hard. Keep taking it even if you feel fine: stopping suddenly can cause serious heart problems.
title: MedlinePlus · Metoprolol

answer: Atorvastatin is a statin. It lowers cholesterol and reduces the risk of a heart attack and stroke. Tell your doctor if you get unexplained muscle pain, tenderness or weakness.
title: MedlinePlus · Atorvastatin

examples: how much tylenol can I take
what can I take for pain
answer: Acetaminophen (Tylenol) is for incision pain. Follow the limit in your discharge papers. Many cold and flu products also contain acetaminophen, so check labels to avoid taking too much.
title: MedlinePlus · Acetaminophen

examples: can I take aleve for pain
answer: Check with your doctor first. If you take aspirin for your heart, MedlinePlus says not to take ibuprofen for pain or fever without talking to your doctor, because it can interfere with aspirin's protection.
title: MedlinePlus · Aspirin

examples: I feel fine do I still need my pills
do I have to take these forever
can I stop my heart pills
answer: Don't stop or change any heart medicine without talking to your care team, even if you feel fine. Some, like metoprolol, can cause serious problems if stopped suddenly.
title: MedlinePlus · Heart bypass surgery, discharge

examples: I forgot to take my pill
what if I miss a dose
answer: Don't take a double dose to catch up unless your pharmacist or care team tells you to. Call your pharmacist: they can tell you what to do for that specific medicine.
title: MedlinePlus · Heart bypass surgery, discharge

examples: my medicine makes me feel weird
answer: Side effects depend on the medicine. Tell your care team or pharmacist about anything new or bothersome. If you feel faint or have chest pain, call 911.
title: MedlinePlus · Heart bypass surgery, discharge

answer: That's really common after heart surgery, and it usually gets better as you heal. Talking with family and friends helps, and so does telling your care team, who can connect you with a counselor. If you ever have thoughts of harming yourself, call or text 988 any time.
title: MedlinePlus · Heart bypass surgery, discharge

examples: I'm worried about another heart attack
answer: Feeling scared after heart surgery is normal. Bypass surgery helps a lot, but it isn't a cure, so taking your medicines, cardiac rehab and a heart-healthy lifestyle all lower your risk. It helps to talk it through with your care team too.
title: NHLBI · What to expect after bypass surgery

examples: is it normal to not sleep
I keep waking up in the middle of the night
answer: Trouble sleeping is common and expected during recovery, and it usually improves. If it keeps going or worries you, mention it to your care team.
title: MedlinePlus · Heart bypass surgery, discharge

examples: how many weeks until I'm back to normal
when will I get my energy back
when will I be myself again
answer: Many people start feeling better after 4 to 6 weeks. Full recovery from traditional bypass surgery can take 6 to 12 weeks or more. You should improve a little each day.
title: American Heart Association · Recovering from heart surgery

examples: is it normal to be tired
why am I so worn out
answer: Tiredness is common after bypass surgery and often eases within 4 to 6 weeks: rest when you're tired. Tiredness that is unusual or getting worse is different, so tell your care team about that.
title: NHLBI · What to expect after bypass surgery

examples: my chest hurts where they cut
answer: Some pain around the chest incision and tightness in the shoulders and upper back are common for several weeks. Chest pain or pressure like angina is different: call 911 for that.
title: NHLBI · What to expect after bypass surgery

examples: my leg is a little swollen
swelling where they took the vein
answer: Some swelling in the leg where the vein was taken is normal for a few weeks. Keep the leg raised when sitting. More swelling, especially in the other leg, is a reason to call your care team the same day.
title: MedlinePlus · Heart bypass surgery, discharge

examples: do I need to use the spirometer
how do I do breathing exercises
do I still need the breathing device
answer: Keep doing the breathing exercises you were taught for 4 to 6 weeks after surgery. They help keep your lungs clear.
title: MedlinePlus · Heart bypass surgery, discharge

examples: how do I check my pulse
how do I take my heart rate
answer: Check your pulse every day, as you were shown. Contact your care team if it's under 60 or over 100 to 120 beats a minute, or feels irregular.
title: MedlinePlus · Heart bypass surgery, discharge

examples: do I need to weigh myself every day
answer: Daily weigh-ins catch fluid building up early. Weigh yourself every morning, after using the bathroom and before breakfast. A gain of 2 pounds in a day or 5 pounds in a week is a reason to call your care team.
title: MedlinePlus · Heart bypass surgery, discharge
